title: Cap. VIII Arg. 10 Resp.: sun not by natural necessity; special ray of mercy not offered to all alike
pass_a_gloss: In many things this comparison fails. First, although God is not inconveniently called a spiritual Sun, yet he does not diffuse his rays by natural necessity, but by voluntary dispensation. Therefore as much as in him he does not diffuse them unto all equally and uniformly. Secondly, though we grant that God diffuses certain common rays of grace unto all and singular (about which matter we will not now litigate), yet that he, as much as in him is, promiscuously offers this special and excellent ray of special mercy unto all and singular, we will never concede.
pass_b_english: The comparison fails in many ways. First: though God is not badly called a spiritual Sun, he does not diffuse his rays by natural necessity but by voluntary dispensation. So as much as in him lies, he does not diffuse them to all equally and uniformly. Second: even if we grant that God diffuses certain common rays of grace to each and all (we will not litigate that now), we will never concede that, as much as in him lies, he promiscuously offers this special excellent ray of special mercy to each and all.
source_text: In multis deficit haec comparatio. Primo, licet Deus haud incommode dicatur Sol spiritualis, tamen non diffundit radios suos naturali necessitate, sed dispensatione voluntaria. Ergo quantum in se non ad omnes aequaliter et uniformiter eos diffundit. Secundo, ut largiamur Deum quosdam communes gratiae radios ad omnes et singulos diffundere (quae de re nunc non litigabimus), tamen specialem hunc et eximium radium specialis misericordiae, quantum in se est, omnibus et singulis promiscue eum praebere, nunquam concedemus.
